dimensions.assessment: Directs the Comptroller General, federal land management agencies, and relevant congressional committees to review cross-boundary wildfire mitigation rules.
dimensions.evidence: directs the Government Accountability Office to study wildfire mitigation across land ownership boundaries and make recommendations

dimensions.assessment: Performs a study and formulates recommendations without directly changing substantive wildfire management rules or operational practices.
dimensions.evidence: To direct the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study on existing programs, rules, and authorities that enable or inhibit wildfire mitigation across land ownership boundaries

dimensions.assessment: Does not specify federal spending authorizations, appropriations, or direct economic impacts.
Mandates a specific study and reporting task for the Government Accountability Office regarding existing federal programs and authorities.
dimensions.evidence: The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a study on--(1) the existing Federal programs, rules, and authorities that enable or inhibit wildfire mitigation

dimensions.assessment: Requires a single report to be submitted not later than 2 years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit... a report

missing_information: The cost of conducting the GAO study.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the Government Accountability Office (Comptroller General) to conduct a study and report on cross-boundary wildfire mitigation programs within a two-year timeframe.
